title: Sweet Geraldine — Warm
description: A playful MIST face family with plump unequal eye masses, offset apertures and compact mouths, using the original Sweet Geraldine sheet as the sole visual reference.
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: MIST robot expression sprite sheet, native raster, five faces on one landscape sheet.
Input image 1 is the PRIMARY and ONLY visual reference: the original later-alligator-sweet-geraldine.png. Use it for the MIST cyan, abstract face grammar, proportions, and the exact five-cell layout. Create a new warmer, playful, hand-shaped graphic cartoon interpretation. This is a targeted correction: the first rendition followed the original silhouettes too closely. The single necessary change is to REINVENT the poses through distinctly hand-shaped asymmetric eye contours and much more compact mouths. The reference supplies ONLY palette, abstract two-eyes-plus-mouth grammar and layout, never exact contours or eye positions. Do not trace or thicken the old rings. Generate at native landscape 1536 x 1024 pixels if possible.

Backdrop: one perfectly flat almost-black background, approximately #050D0C, filling the entire canvas. Every visible face feature is one solid pale turquoise MIST cyan matched to the original reference, with its slightly greenish cyan character; avoid shifting it toward saturated blue. Crisp smooth contours with no lighting effects.

Composition: EXACTLY FIVE separate faces, laid out in an invisible 3-column by 2-row grid of equal cells. Top-left attentive, top-middle considering, top-right skeptical; bottom-left amused, bottom-middle concerned; bottom-right entirely empty background. Each face remains comfortably inside its own cell with generous margins for CSS clipping. All faces are at comparable scale; loosely center them in their cells. Keep each face about 330 pixels wide and no more than 240 pixels tall; keep each mouth only 45–70 pixels wide, with ample breathing room around its features. No separators, no borders, no drawn grid.

Core face grammar: each face has EXACTLY TWO cyan eyes plus ONE compact cyan mouth, and absolutely no other feature. No enclosing head or body. Eyes are expressive, plump, irregular open-C graphic masses: the dark aperture runs openly to the exterior, not a closed ring with a pupil. Use lively unequal C shapes, offset eye heights, and hand-shaped smooth contour asymmetry. Each C should have a plump pear-like or bean-like outside silhouette, a lopsided inner aperture, and unequal upper/lower mass. Deliberately avoid concentric circular outside and inside edges. Personality comes entirely from the eye masses, their open apertures and integrated eyelid contours, plus the mouth placement. Coordinate both eyes so each pair acts out its expression together; do not make five sets of perfect rings. Keep rounded tips and broadly rounded cartoon curves. Invent meaningfully different pose shapes within this grammar, not simply thicker versions of the reference rings.

Five required expressions:
1. ATTENTIVE, top-left: eager warmth. Two strongly uneven open C eyes; one is a higher tall plump pear-shaped C with a small lopsided inner opening, while the opposite eye is a shorter sideways bean-shaped C with a wider tilted inner opening. Offset both sizes and heights so it clearly differs from the old ring pair. Both feel openly engaged. Compact shallow curved smile, a little off-center. Friendly and eager, not manic.
2. CONSIDERING, top-middle: genuine uncertain thoughtfulness. One pronounced tall C eye with a swollen lower cheek of the eye mass and sharply unequal rim widths, leaning slightly outward, and one much shorter low oblique C with a sleepy but open aperture. Shift the taller eye closer to the middle of its cell than in the reference and rotate the shorter eye gently outward. Their unequal silhouettes visibly lean into uncertainty. A very small mostly flat wry mouth with just one subtle kink, placed off-center. No broad grin or cheerful smile.
3. SKEPTICAL, top-right: clear skeptical side-eye within the warm graphic family. One eye is a short broad sideways C mass with a low oblique flattened integrated lid and narrow aperture; the opposite eye is a tall raised open C whose bulbous top and skinny bottom create a lopsided inner opening. Deliberately change both outside silhouettes from the original. This contrast must be immediately readable. One compact mouth with a gentle downward diagonal slope, off-center. No additional eyebrow, no anger, no smile.
4. AMUSED, bottom-left: playful delight. One eye is a broad squashed bean-shaped C, tipped joyfully inward; the other is a plump lopsided C with a laughing, much narrower curved aperture still visibly cut openly into its connected eye mass. It must remain one connected C eye, never a detached eyebrow-like arch. Clear asymmetric laughter, not another pair of ordinary circles. One compact open smiling bowl or bean-shaped mouth, solid cyan, with no teeth or tongue and no extra detached mark.
5. CONCERNED, bottom-middle: soft empathetic concern. Uneven softened drooped open C eyes with mostly closed sloping apertures and eyelids integrated into the eye silhouettes. Make their outer eye silhouettes unequal soft bean shapes, not circles, and make one eye lower and wider than the other. The inner upper edges rise gently toward each other while outer portions droop, so the face reads comforting and worried rather than angry. One tiny closed downturned curve mouth. It must be visibly downturned, not smiling.

Style: warm, appealing, hand-shaped graphic cartoon, like thoughtfully posed clean cartoon facial cutouts. Slightly uneven plump eye masses and asymmetric apertures; strong emotion through silhouette. Retain the original's simple abstract MIST identity. Clean native raster artwork, no texture.

Strict exclusions: no glow, neon halo, gradients, shading, reflections, noise, paper grain, brush texture, pupils, irises, noses, cheeks, cheek dots, blush, floating eyebrows, ears, teeth, tongues, limbs, bodily features, alligator anatomy, props, screens, frames, text, labels, symbols, logos, watermarks, extra marks, or sixth face. Only the fifteen cyan features against a uniform flat dark background. Bottom-right cell stays completely empty.

qa.inspection: Full native output inspected with view_image.
qa.repairReason: The first generation kept four eye poses too close to the original; the selected repair materially changed the hand-shaped silhouettes while keeping palette, face grammar and layout.
qa.layout: Exactly five faces in the original invisible 3-column by 2-row positions. Bottom-right remains empty and every face stays within its cell with generous margins.
qa.featureCount: Each face has two eye masses and one compact mouth; no additional bodily features, props, labels, teeth or tongue.
qa.attentive: Tall plump raised C paired with a lower broad sideways C and a shallow compact smile. Reads as friendly engagement.
qa.considering: Strong tall-versus-short eye contrast, offset heights and a small mostly flat wry mouth. Reads as uncertain thoughtfulness.
qa.skeptical: Clearly flattened low lid on one side, raised open C opposite, and a compact downward-sloping mouth. Skepticism remains clear.
qa.amused: Two differently tilted rounded C masses with an open bowl smile. Playful, though the laughing-eye aperture is broader than requested.
qa.concerned: Uneven sloping integrated lids with inward-raised edges and a compact downturned mouth. Concern is visible, with a more tense left corner than the softest intended version.
qa.style: Materially different plump asymmetric silhouettes, pale cyan on greenish near-black. No visible glow, gradients, pupils or added decorative marks.

limitations: The concerned face's right eye has a closed dark aperture rather than a clearly exterior-opening C.
The amused eye pair reads playful but does not fully achieve the requested narrow laughing aperture.
The concerned left inner lid has a pointed corner that makes the pose tenser than the intended gentle comfort.
Native image generation produces small color variations; the cyan and dark background are visually close to the reference rather than a mathematically exact flat palette.
